subject: Film & Cinema
title: Found Footage: When the Camera Lies
description: A fast breakdown of Found Footage: When the Camera Lies for builders.

hook.text: The Blair Witch Project cost $60,000 and convinced millions it was real footage.

buildup.text: Found footage films mimic amateur recordings to make horror feel authentic and intimate.

discovery.text: The shaky camera and lack of music trick the brain into treating fiction as reality.

twist.text: Overuse drained the gimmick, but Paranormal Activity proved it still worked in 2007.

climax.text: Found footage showed that less production value can mean more fear.

punchline.text: The cheapest camera tells the scariest story.

quiz.question: Why does found footage horror feel scarier to audiences?
options: The amateur style tricks the brain into feeling it's real
